profile.headline: Bioinformatics Software Engineer
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary: I am a software developer supporting the development, running and maintenance of alignment and variant calling workflows for liquid biopsy assays in the Marie-Josée and Henry R. Kravis Center for Molecular Oncology (CMO).

positions.title: Bioinformatics Software Engineer III
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
•    Designed and developed a Spring Boot and PostgreSQL microservice that maps patient identifiers to sample file locations and associated metadata. Replaced fragile lookup scripts with a queryable REST API used by downstream services and research teams.
•    Extended a distributed workflow orchestration platform built on Django microservices to support additional workflow languages, new pipelines, and expanded API endpoints, deployed to production through GitHub Actions CI validation.
•    Reduced pipeline failures across an orchestration database of ~8,000 samples by triaging and resolving issues spanning input data integrity, tool errors, CPU and memory resource configuration, and orchestration logic.
•    Built and deployed containerized, reproducible production workflows (Nextflow, CWL) for variant calling and quality-control analysis supporting cfDNA sequencing assays, enabling scalable execution across a shared HPC cluster.
•    Co-led a working group of engineers and scientists in adopting shared module standards, maintaining a common open-source repository and driving adoption through documentation, workshops, and internal presentations.

positions.title: Data Scientist
positions.description:
•    Credited author on EdSurvey, an open-source R package distributed on CRAN, implementing new class methods, optimizing performance-critical routines in C, and managing release submissions and public repository maintenance.
•    Designed and developed an automated data pipeline (Airflow, Python, MySQL) that replaced a legacy SAS and Excel process, producing a queryable database of Common Core education data.
•    Co-developed In-Compass, an interactive R Shiny application enabling non-technical users to explore and analyze international large-scale assessment data.

positions.title: Researcher
positions.description: Developed a prototype model to assist in the detection of anomalous blood pressures taken from less accurate electronic devices using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data. Model predictions provided baseline estimate to assess the validity of in-office blood pressure measurements.

positions.title: Applied Statistics Tutor
positions.description: Help students understand topics such as the expected value and variance of distributions, and regression (Linear, Logistic, and Poisson). Troubleshoot issues with R and data manipulation.

positions.title: Doobie DJ
positions.description: Prepare a weekly talk show on Movies and Music. Help coordinate Doobie Palooza, an entirely student run music festival.

positions.title: Data Science Intern
positions.description: Designed a hurdle model that improved the classification of risky clients based on claim size as compared to standard linear regression.

positions.title: Author/Analyst
positions.description:
Investigate empirical social and institutional patterns at Denison University using surveys and a variety of other data sources: 
- Accessed campus swipe data to determine the busiest gym times, and identify those most likely to be there. 
- Employed survey data to quantify student support for the use of more surveillance on campus, and identify what predicted support.
